app.title: University Simulator
app.tagline: Rehearse your first semester before it's real.
home.hook: About 620 000 NSFAS-funded first-years in 2023. Only about 130 000 were still funded a year later.
home.what: Play eight weeks of your first university semester in about 10 minutes. Juggle money, marks and wellbeing through the crises first-years really face, then keep a survival plan for real life.
home.privacy: No account and no sign-up. Your answers stay on this device.
home.offline: You're offline. The game still works.
home.f1.title: Three meters
home.f1.body: Money, marks and wellbeing. Every choice trades one against another.
home.f2.title: Real campus support
home.f2.body: Seeking help reveals the actual service at your university and how to reach it.
home.f3.title: A plan you keep
home.f3.body: A budget built on your real income, a late-allowance playbook and your support contacts.

tier.gap.title: Your money doesn't cover the basics
tier.gap.body: Basics cost about {essentials} a month where you'll live, and you have {income}: a gap of {gap}. That's a funding problem, not a budgeting failure. No split can fix it, but these steps can help:
tier.gap.step1: Register for campus food support in week 1, before money runs out.
tier.gap.step2: Ask the financial aid office if you qualify for more: NSFAS, bursaries or hardship funds.
tier.gap.step3: Look for a few hours a week of campus work that won't hurt your studies.
tier.gap.step4: Cut costs together: cook in groups, share data bundles, buy books second-hand.
tier.gap.step5: Talk honestly with family about what's possible, and when.
tier.tight.title: Just enough, with no room for surprises
tier.tight.body: Your money covers the basics ({essentials}) with {surplus} to spare. One late payment or surprise cost will push you short, so build a small buffer first.
tier.ok.title: Basics covered, with some room
tier.ok.body: You have {surplus} a month above the basics. Put part of it into a buffer before spending on extras.
tier.strong.title: You're well covered
tier.strong.body: You have {surplus} a month above the basics. Build a buffer of at least a month, and set a limit for social spending so it doesn't creep up.

intro.1.title: First year is where students fall out
intro.1.body: About 620 000 NSFAS-funded first-years in 2023. Only about 130 000 were still funded a year later. The crises behind it are predictable: late allowances, rent, family requests and test-week stress.
intro.2.title: Rehearse it before it's real
intro.2.body: Set up your real situation, then play 8 weeks in about 10 minutes. Each week brings one situation and two or three choices. Watch your money, marks and wellbeing, and ask for help to see the support campuses offer.
intro.3.title: Your journey, chapter by chapter
intro.3.body: Start with Arrival or First Term, then follow your journey all the way to graduation. After every chapter, a Semester Forecast predicts your riskiest weeks and builds a survival plan to save or share on WhatsApp. No account, and it works offline.

home.title: University Simulator
home.about: Rehearse university before it's real. Create your student, live through the moments that push South African students out (late allowances, family requests, test weeks, loneliness), and see what support exists before you need it.
home.about2: After every chapter, a Semester Forecast reads your choices, predicts your riskiest weeks and builds a survival plan you can keep.
home.card.setupNew: Create your student: university, course, home, money and more. Takes about a minute.
home.card.firstDesc: Arrival, First Term, First Exams and Bounce Back: the year most students find hardest.
home.card.middleDesc: Second and third year: old fees, moving off campus, choosing a major, side hustles and burnout.
home.card.finalDesc: Final-year projects, job applications, old debts and graduation day.
why.title: Getting in is not the hard part. Staying in is.
why.stat1: About 620 000 NSFAS-funded first-years in 2023. Only about 130 000 were still funded a year later.
why.stat2: Some estimates suggest as many as 60% of first-years leave after their first term.
why.stat2src: Source: Fundi CEO, quoted by EWN
why.i1: Allowances that arrive late, and rent due before the money
why.i2: Family asking for money you need yourself
why.i3: No laptop, no data, or a long commute
why.i4: Being far from home, and lonely
why.i5: Tests and assignments that all land in the same week
why.i7: Working, or caring for someone, while you study
why.i8: A failed module, or old fees that block registration
why.everyone: This is for everyone: NSFAS, bursary, family-funded or paying your own way; straight from school or coming back older; in res, renting or commuting; first year or already in second year. These crises are predictable, and so is the help.
how.title: Rehearse it, then keep the plan
how.s1: Your real situation: university, course, housing, funding, money, home and responsibilities. The game is built from it.
how.s2t: Play your year, week by week
how.s2: Each week brings a real situation and two or three choices. Watch your money, marks and wellbeing. You can change an answer straight after you make it.
how.s3: Choose to get help and you'll see the kind of service campuses offer, what it does and how to reach it.
how.s4: After every chapter, the Semester Forecast predicts your riskiest weeks and builds a survival plan to save or share on WhatsApp.
how.note: Between steps there is a break, where you can stop and come back later. Sometimes it holds a quick optional question: those are not part of the main story and never change your money, marks or wellbeing. No account. Works offline. About 10 minutes for First Term.
home.cardsLead: Create your character, then play any part of the journey: learners still deciding, first-years and students already in second year are all welcome.

about.title: About University Simulator
about.lead: A short game where South African students rehearse university life before it happens.
about.p1: You set up a student like you, play short chapters from matric to graduation, and juggle money, marks and wellbeing. Every hard moment has a way through, and there are wins along the way.
about.p2: After every chapter, a Semester Forecast reads your choices and builds a survival plan you can keep. The forecast uses clear, research-based rules, not a trained AI model.
about.independent: Sizwe University is fictional. This app is independent, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by any university.
about.advice: This is not professional, financial, legal or medical advice. For urgent help, use the national helplines shown in the app.
about.numbers: Amounts, rules and dates are examples. Check the real ones with your university and your funder.
uni.title: Your campus, in the game
uni.lead: The demo uses a fictional campus. A licensed version gives your students a rehearsal of your university, with your services and your costs.
uni.s1: Every card, cost and support service is data. Your pack names your real offices, how to reach them and what things cost near your campus.
uni.s2: Your Student Affairs team checks every support card and the sensitive content before students see it. Updates reach students without a new app.
uni.s3: You see how many students completed each chapter and what they said. No names, no logins and no student records.
uni.s4: Licences are per institution and per year, in tiers by student numbers. The Sizwe demo campus stays free to try.
uni.contact: We are looking for one or two universities to pilot a campus version in 2027. Speak to the team that showed you this app.
privacy.title: Privacy, in plain language
privacy.lead: There is no account and no login. We never ask for your name, number or student number.
privacy.p1: Your setup answers, choices and progress are stored on this device only.
privacy.p2: Campus Realities is never tracked. Nothing about what you open there is saved or sent, even on your own device.
privacy.p3: When you finish a chapter and you are online, the app may send an anonymous count: a random device code and the chapter name. Feedback answers are sent only if you tap Send.
privacy.p4: If the AI-written plan is switched on, only your forecast numbers are sent to write it. No names, and nothing you typed.
privacy.p5: Sharing your survival plan is your choice, and it goes only where you send it.
privacy.erased: Everything on this device was erased.

cr.note: Content note: these topics include discrimination and sexual violence. Read at your own pace, and leave whenever you want. Free, confidential help is available now:
